newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Eurolira volatility begins to rise again.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Eurolira volatility begins to rise again.

text.p: Implied volatility for options on Eurolira futures traded on LIFFE was better bid on Friday with good buying activity in the front month, brokers said.

Earlier in the week volatility fell sharply after the Bank of Italy cut its key discount rate to 6.75 percent from 7.50 percent. Many have started to hedge short positions in Eurolire calls, dealers said.
"A lot of people have been buying at- and out-of-the-money calls in Eurolire, because we had the rate cut," said Ian Aubrey, head of futures and options sales at Yamaichi International in London.
Brokers quoted implied volatility at around 16.0 percent for March, 16.9 percent for June and 20 percent for September.
When the session opened vol levels were at 14.74 percent for March, 15.95 percent for June and 19.4 percent for September.
Luke White, broker at Fimat Futures UK said in vol terms, June was now the important month.

"In talking about volatility people tend to talk about June because the March vol is getting more and more discounted, particularly since the cut a couple of day's ago," he said. "Everyone knows, or think they know, where the rates are going to be."
White said implied volatilty levels had been pushed up partly by March call buying, with notable interest in 93.50 and 93.75 strikes.
In the underlying market, the March Eurolira future is currently trading at 93.31, up two basis points on the day, while the June Eurolira future was down 0.02 at 93.86.
Activity throughout the options market was expected to pick up in the afternoon, Aubrey said, with European markets taking a lead from the U.S. bond market.

"It's the end of the week and I sense that some shorts could get washed out ahead of the weekend," he said. "And we've got the important (U.S.) employment cost index coming out on Tuesday which a lot of traders are nervous about."
